item.title: Make wait_time agree exactly with try_acquire after the wait
item.brief:
Follow-up to the rate limiter just committed (commit 502a89a on archon/d3bht145-implement-token-bucket-rate-limiter-per). Spec `SPEC.md` says `wait_time(n)` returns the seconds until `try_acquire(n)` would succeed. The implementer reported that float rounding can leave the bucket just below `n` tokens right after the returned delay, so the first retry of `try_acquire` may still return False.

Goal: make `wait_time(n)` and `try_acquire(n)` agree exactly: once the bucket's clock has advanced by the returned `wait_time`, `try_acquire(n)` must return True. Verify this first with a test (advance the injected clock by exactly `wait_time` and check), then fix the arithmetic in `ratelimit.py` (for example compute the delay so the refill reaches `n` exactly, or use a small documented tolerance only if exact is not possible). Do not change behaviour otherwise; keep all existing tests passing and add the regression test to `test_ratelimit.py`.

Constraints: standard library only; do not edit `SPEC.md`; do not add type checks (out of scope); commit the work on the working branch.

evidence.caption: Advance-by-wait regression on the implementation before the fix (ceb82d2 + new tests)

pr.body:
Approach: wait_time estimates the delay from the refill rate, then nudges it up by max(ulp(now+wait), ulp(wait)) until _tokens_at(now+wait) >= n, using the same clock-advance arithmetic as try_acquire. _refill and _tokens_at share one refill expression. wait_time also counts the gap when the clock has gone backwards.

Key files: ratelimit.py (TokenBucket.wait_time, _refill, _tokens_at, _seconds_until). test_ratelimit.py: advance-by-wait regression (four cases), negative-clock regression (199 subtests), backwards-clock gap test.

Checks: unittest on ceb82d2 implementation with new tests: 3 advance-by-wait subtests failed. On ccc7043: 19 tests OK. Random sweep 150k cases with clock offsets from -3 to 1e9: 0 failures.

Base note: the implementation commit 502a89a lives on archon/d3bht145; it was cherry-picked here as ceb82d2 so this branch has code to fix.

Assumptions: the wait is exact only for clocks where the caller advances by adding the returned value to the current clock reading. Review: re-review of 573df3c..ccc7043 passed; the first review failed on a negative-clock RuntimeError, fixed in ccc7043.
pr.summary: made wait_time(n) exact: after advancing the clock by it, try_acquire(n) succeeds. now also counts the clock-backwards gap. before: first retry could fail by float rounding (3 of 4 reproducer cases; ~19% of random cases); now: 0 failures in 150k random cases incl. negative clocks.
pr.title: Make wait_time agree exactly with try_acquire

agt_01M8GR1357XZ4HXRHMGQEJ6CSF:1.description: wait_time raises RuntimeError on a valid negative clock after a backward jump; the nudge loop steps by ulp of the target clock value, which is a no-op on wait when |now+wait| << |wait|. Repro: clock 0 -> -2.0 with TokenBucket(1, 0.7) gives 380/999 RuntimeErrors. Scratch test: max(ulp(now+wait), ulp(wait)) gives 0 failures in both regimes. at ratelimit.py:75

agt_01M8GR1357XZ4HXRHMGQEJ6CSF:2.description: No test covers the negative-clock / backward-jump regime or the RuntimeError path, so the bug above passes the 18-test suite. Add a test with the clock at a negative value, advancing by wait_time and asserting try_acquire succeeds. at test_ratelimit.py:119

agt_01M8GR1357XZ4HXRHMGQEJ6CSF:3.description: _seconds_until comment is 4 lines; CLAUDE.md allows at most 2 lines per comment. at ratelimit.py:68

risk.why: Contained behaviour change to wait_time in a rate limiter: values change by ulps and the backwards-clock case now counts the gap. No security, persistence or concurrency. Reviewers rated it medium.

item.title: Implement token-bucket rate limiter per SPEC.md in ratelimit.py
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim): "Implement the rate limiter described in `SPEC.md` in `ratelimit.py` (the module currently only has stubs). Follow the spec exactly, including its error cases and edge cases; the tests in `test_ratelimit.py` only cover the basics. Keep it dependency-free (standard library only) and commit your work."

Goal: implement `TokenBucket` and `KeyedLimiter` in `ratelimit.py` exactly as `SPEC.md` states. The spec is the source of truth: every error case (ValueError on invalid capacity, refill_per_sec, max_keys, n), the start-full rule, the capacity cap, fractional tokens, `wait_time` semantics (no consumption), the clock-goes-backwards rule, and the LRU eviction rule (both try_acquire and wait_time count as a use; evicted keys return full) must hold.

Constraints:
- Standard library only. Keep the injected `clock` as the only time source.
- Do not edit SPEC.md.
- Keep `test_ratelimit.py` passing. You may add tests for the spec's edge cases and error cases to it.
- Keep functions small and readable; validate inputs at the constructor and method boundaries.
- Commit the work on the working branch with a clear message.

pr.body: Approach: ratelimit.py holds a lazy-refill TokenBucket (tokens and last-seen time, refilled on each call from the injected clock; clock not advancing leaves state unchanged) and a KeyedLimiter with an OrderedDict of buckets (move_to_end on use, popitem(last=False) on overflow). Validation of capacity, refill_per_sec, max_keys and n happens before any state change, so a rejected call creates no key. Checks: unittest 16 tests OK; ruff clean. Review: pass, no blocking findings. Follow-ups: float rounding after wait_time delay; no explicit type checks (TypeError for non-numerics, non-integer max_keys accepted).
